profile.reading:
Data Foundry is a privately held Texas colocation operator. This facility, formally labeled Data Foundry 00 and marketed as Austin 1, sits at 7401 East Ben White Boulevard, Suite 1000, Austin, Texas 78741, in Travis County, less than seven minutes from Austin Bergstrom International Airport by Data Foundry's own description. It is roughly 2.5 kilometers from the operator's separate Data Foundry 01 and 02 buildings on the shared Data Ranch campus, which this registry treats as confirmation that Austin 1 is a genuinely distinct third Austin facility rather than an alternate name for either of those two buildings.

The operator's own dedicated page for the facility describes a 40,000 square foot building sited in what it calls a low risk natural disaster zone, powered by three 1,500 kilowatt Caterpillar diesel generators providing 4.5 megawatts of combined backup generation, with 6,000 gallons of onsite fuel giving about 48 hours of runtime at N+1 redundancy. Two 3,000 amp, 480 volt automatic transfer switches and a UPS bank made up of four 500 kVA and three 550 kVA units back two independent power feeds fed from separate substations. Cooling runs on 30 ton Liebert computer room air conditioners at N+1 redundancy paired with 78 ton Liebert glycol condensing units at N+4 redundancy, on a chilled water system the operator describes as concurrently maintainable. Data Foundry lists more than 15 network providers on site through a blended internet service guaranteeing access to at least four carriers at once, plus its own CloudTap service for direct connections to major cloud platforms. Physical security includes seven layers of protection, concrete filled steel reinforced perimeter barriers, biometric access controls and man traps, and continuous motion activated video surveillance. The facility carries SSAE 18, HIPAA, and AICPA compliance along with ISO 27001 certification and PCI DSS certified status.

Data Foundry has operated in Texas for more than two decades, with its Austin presence now spanning three non adjacent buildings, this one plus the Data Ranch campus, and one additional Houston facility tracked separately in this registry. As an independent Texas company that does not file SEC disclosures, Data Foundry's specifications here are sourced solely to its own published materials rather than any independent audit. No year opened date was located for this facility in sourcing reviewed this session. East Ben White Boulevard sits south of downtown Austin along US 71, a corridor that has drawn light industrial and logistics tenants distinct from the Domain and North Austin corridor favored by several other hyperscale developments tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
Data Foundry Austin 1 occupies 40,000 square feet of technical space in Travis County, Texas. The operator has not published a power figure for this facility, so no IT load, critical load, or UPS capacity is on record here. Without a megawatt number, no rack-count or accelerator estimate can be responsibly derived.

The absence of a published power figure also places this campus outside the 13 Texas facilities for which this site holds capacity data, meaning it does not contribute to the 389 MW total mapped across the state. The state context ranks it 14th by published megawatts, but that ranking reflects the absence of a figure rather than a measured position, because any facility without a published number sorts below all 13 that have one. Texas has 133 mapped facilities in total, and the majority of those publish no power specification, so Austin 1 is typical of the state in that regard.

For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI workloads, the 40,000 square feet of technical space signals a mid-sized colocation facility rather than a hyperscale build, but floor area alone does not determine AI suitability. Power density per rack and total available power are the constraints that govern whether a site can support GPU clusters, and neither figure is published here. Until the operator publishes a power specification, this campus cannot be evaluated against the grid-constrained scaling thesis that defines AI infrastructure relevance.
